topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: A unit test states a behavioral claim about a small component under controlled conditions. Harbor’s count parser accepts a precise decimal grammar and range; testing it means identifying both the permitted values and the representations that must be rejected. The goal is not to maximize the number of assertions indiscriminately, but to make failures local, reproducible, and informative.

topics.title: 6.1.1 Structuring Test Cases
topics.summary: Arrange the input and dependencies, perform one meaningful operation, and examine the result. A case should make its purpose visible: minimum valid count, maximum valid count, empty text, overflow, or trailing garbage. Several assertions can belong to one case when they describe the same outcome, but an unrelated cascade obscures the first broken contract.

topics.summary: Specify success values and failure categories. A test that only checks that something threw may accept the wrong exception from a setup bug. Likewise, a nonempty output string is weaker evidence than the exact expected record when the format is part of the API.

topics.title: 6.2.1 Testing Boundary Conditions
topics.summary: Boundaries divide behavior classes. For a range from zero through 65,535, test both endpoints, neighbors, and representations near conversion overflow. Empty and single-character inputs exercise paths that large ordinary values can miss. A fixed maximum length is another boundary independent of the numeric maximum.

topics.title: 6.2.2 Testing Error Paths
topics.summary: A failure path is part of the public contract. Verify that rejected input does not leave partially mutated state, leak an owned resource, or return a success-like sentinel that callers cannot distinguish from a legitimate value. Prefer explicit error results when failure is routine data validation.

topics.title: Trace the implementation
topics.summary: The parser’s grammar explicitly permits leading zeroes within five characters and rejects signs and whitespace. Those decisions are visible in the table rather than inherited accidentally from a conversion function. The range includes zero because this is a numeric port-field parser; a connection policy may separately prohibit zero for a remote destination.

topics.title: Solution and review notes
topics.summary: An embedded NUL is not the end of a string_view when its length includes that byte; the character check rejects it. This catches assumptions inherited from null-terminated C strings. Non-ASCII bytes are rejected by direct comparisons without passing a negative char to a cctype function.
